```{python}
import importlib.metadata
import json
import os
import platform
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from guides import __version__
from guides.analysis import analyse
from guides.data import ROOT, SETTINGS
from guides.plot import locus_figure

request = json.loads(Path(os.environ["GUIDES_REQUEST"]).read_text())
result = analyse(request)
table, gene = result["table"], result["gene"]
placed = table[table.status == "placed"]
display(Markdown(f"## {gene['gene']} · K562\n\n"
    f"**Question:** how does local regulatory context differ between guides targeting {gene['gene']}?\n\n"
    f"Input: **{request['mode']}**. Reference: **GRCh38**, annotation: **GENCODE v32**. "
    f"Of **{len(table)}** submitted guides, **{len(placed)}** have exactly one matching "
    f"spacer plus NGG PAM in the target search interval, **{int((table.status == 'not found').sum())}** "
    f"have none, and **{int((table.status == 'ambiguous').sum())}** have multiple matches. "
    "This is local placement, not a genome-wide specificity test."))
```

## Locus map

```{python}
#| label: fig-locus
#| fig-cap: "Called K562 peaks above a shared gene-and-guide panel. Guide colours identify inputs, not efficacy; black tips with white edges mark PAMs. Orange intervals and grey shading show windows around annotated target-gene transcript starts. The dashed line is the GENCODE start nearest the midpoint of the placed-guide span (or the view midpoint if none are placed), also identified in the title. The axis shows distance from that start in the target gene's direction, with downstream to the right. Grey peak bars show presence, not signal height. Only unambiguously placed guides are drawn."
#| fig-alt: "Four compact K562 peak tracks above coloured guide bars with black PAM tips, an orange promoter strip and gene arrows. A dashed TSS line and promoter shading align across the panels."
figure = locus_figure(result)
display(figure)
```

## Guide placement

Guide numbers follow input order; they are not efficacy ranks. Coordinates in this
table are **1-based, inclusive**. The spacer is written in its own 5′–3′ orientation;
the strand tells how it maps to the reference. All alternative exact placements
are retained in `placements.csv` using **0-based, half-open** coordinates.

```{python}
placement = table[["guide", "sequence", "status", "matches", "start", "end", "strand", "pam"]].copy()
for column in ["start", "end"]:
    placement[column] = placement[column].map(lambda n: "—" if pd.isna(n) else f"{n:.0f}")
display(Markdown(placement.fillna("—").to_markdown(index=False)))
```

## Regulatory context

Overlap is the number of reference bases shared by a **spacer plus its PAM** and
the union of called peaks. Overlapping peaks are not counted twice. TSS distance
is measured from the spacer midpoint to the nearest annotated transcript start
of the target gene; positive means downstream in the **gene's** orientation.
CTCF distance is the minimum gap between the guide footprint and a called CTCF
peak on the same chromosome; touching intervals have zero gap.

```{python}
columns = ["guide", "tss_distance_bp", "promoter_bp", "DNase_bp", "H3K4me3_bp", "H3K27ac_bp", "CTCF_bp", "nearest_CTCF_bp"]
display(Markdown(table[columns].fillna("—").to_markdown(index=False, floatfmt=".1f")))
if len(placed):
    counts = {key: int((placed[f"{key}_bp"] > 0).sum()) for key in result["tracks"]}
    display(Markdown(f"Among the **{len(placed)}** placed guides, **{counts['DNase']}** overlap "
        f"a called DNase peak, **{counts['H3K4me3']}** an H3K4me3 peak, "
        f"**{counts['H3K27ac']}** an H3K27ac peak and **{counts['CTCF']}** a CTCF peak. "
        "These are descriptive annotations of the selected reference datasets."))
else:
    display(Markdown("No guide has an unambiguous placement, so no regulatory comparison can be made."))
```

Differences here identify candidate contextual differences; they do not establish
why guides behave differently. Shared context also does not establish equal
efficacy. ENCODE measurements come from separate K562 experiments, not from cells
treated with these guides. An uncalled peak is not proof of absent activity or
binding. Annotated transcript starts need not be the active starts in K562.
No expression, knockdown, off-target activity or CTCF-motif result is inferred.

## Methods and reproducibility

```{python}
start, end = result["manifest"]["search_interval"]
display(Markdown(f"The exact-match search covers **{gene['chrom']}:{start + 1:,}–{end:,}** "
    f"(the annotated gene plus **{SETTINGS['search_flank']:,} bp** on each side, clipped to the reference). "
    "Both strands are searched for the input spacer and a compatible NGG PAM. "
    f"Target-promoter windows extend **{SETTINGS['promoter_upstream']:,} bp upstream** and "
    f"**{SETTINGS['promoter_downstream']:,} bp downstream** of each GENCODE basic transcript start. "
    f"The figure adds **{SETTINGS['plot_flank']:,} bp** on either side of the placed spacers. "
    "Unknown bases, mismatches, bulges, other PAMs and alternative assembly contigs are not searched."))
```

All tables, measurements and the figure are recomputed in this Quarto render.
The raw files are downloaded by code, checked against committed checksums and
kept read-only. Input sequences, settings, source URLs and SHA-256 checksums are
saved beside the results in `provenance.json`. The demonstration is rebuilt with
`pixi install --locked` followed by `pixi run reproduce`.

## Sources and terms

This report develops the locus-annotation part of **One gene, four guides**, the
author's CBIO7102 coursework. The implementation is standalone and uses public
reference data; no MBZUAI account is needed.

```{python}
sources = result["manifest"]["sources"]
for source in sources:
    label = source.get("accession", source["filename"])
    display(Markdown(f"- **{source['key']}**: [{label}]({source['citation_url']}). "
                     f"[{source['license']}]({source['license_url']})."))
```

GENCODE: Frankish et al. (2019), [doi:10.1093/nar/gky955](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gky955).
ENCODE Project Consortium (2012), [doi:10.1038/nature11247](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature11247).
